mechanisms.name: Abstract interfaces
mechanisms.summary: Hide representations while exporting observations and laws for client proofs.

mechanisms.name: Refinements
mechanisms.summary: Express preconditions, postconditions, and datatype invariants in types.

mechanisms.name: Runtime checks and testing
mechanisms.summary: Check refinements with `assume_`, then use the facts in proofs and executable tests.

mechanisms.name: Heap ownership and framing
mechanisms.summary: Track permission to read and update a heap fragment while preserving the rest.

mechanisms.name: Borrowing with prophecies
mechanisms.summary: Name a loan’s eventual contents and relate them to the owner returned afterward. Creating and ending a loan are not total.

mechanisms.name: Ownership transfer and parallelism
mechanisms.summary: Transfer exclusive resources through channels or give parallel callbacks disjoint slices.

mechanisms.name: Atomic invariants
mechanisms.summary: Exchange protected resources at atomic events while maintaining a shared invariant.

mechanisms.name: Time credits and amortized analysis
mechanisms.summary: Use consumable ghost budgets and potentials to bound charged operations.

mechanisms.name: Definitions and induction
mechanisms.summary: Unfold equations with `[@def]` and prove recursive properties by induction.

mechanisms.name: Totality
mechanisms.summary: Check termination and definedness for specification functions and erasable proofs.

mechanisms.name: Ghost code and erasure
mechanisms.summary: Use checked proofs without executing them; erase evidence from runtime representations.

mechanisms.name: Inductive definitions
mechanisms.summary: Relations defined by inference rules, written as ordinary variants whose fields carry the premises as refinements. Today such relations are written by hand as a derivation datatype with a validity predicate; this needs fields whose refinements mention earlier fields.

mechanisms.name: Applying laws automatically
mechanisms.summary: Clients call an abstract structure's laws by hand, which is most of their proof lines. Z3 quantifiers would apply them automatically but make proofs sensitive to unrelated edits; Vox could instead instantiate a declared set of laws itself on matching terms. Whether either is worth its cost in predictability is open.

mechanisms.name: Sizes of in-memory data
mechanisms.summary: Machine integers wrap in the logic and ghost code can build lists of any length, so facts such as distinct row numbers need a size premise. A mode for values only run-time code can produce would let the checker bound them; whether that is worth a new mode is open.

mechanisms.name: Termination of stateful code
mechanisms.summary: `total` means terminating without raising. It covers pure code and writes through uniquely owned storage (`Slice.set` writes a unique slice), but not borrowing, whose loans are created and ended by operations that are not total, nor code built on the typed heap, such as the hash table, the rings or Hindley–Milner inference: their state is uniquely owned, but `Pref.read` and `write` are declared partial. A termination guarantee for such code would be a separate mode.

mechanisms.name: Code that both proves and runs
mechanisms.summary: Some demos keep a certificate-producing and an erased version of the same function. Polymorphism over whether a value is ghost would let one definition serve both, at the cost of a deeper mode system.
